issues.description: push_error is called with a string but likely expects an ErrorFrame
issues.detail: The PR description says 'Add error frame for all error types,' but push_error is called with error_msg as a positional string. In pipecat, push_error typically expects an ErrorFrame instance. If the prior code paths worked, fine — but the unified branch now routes many new message types through the same call, so any signature mismatch will silently fail for all of them. Verify push_error's signature.

issues.description: Logging of error events was dropped in the consolidation
issues.detail: The previous code logged each error type via logger.error before pushing the error frame. The new unified branch only calls push_error and removes the logger.error lines. This reduces observability — operators tailing logs will no longer see ElevenLabs errors unless push_error itself logs. Restore a logger.error(f"ElevenLabs {message_type}: {error_msg}") line.
'transcriber_error' appears twice in the message_type tuple (lines 727 and 731 of the new code). Harmless but sloppy — suggests the list was assembled by hand without dedup. Remove the duplicate.

issues.description: Removing the outer try/except may surface exceptions that previously self-healed
issues.detail: Before: _receive_messages swallowed all exceptions from the async-for loop and logged a warning, letting the websocket_service reconnect cleanly. Now any non-disconnect exception (e.g., transient json decode at a deeper layer, asyncio.CancelledError handling) will propagate up. Confirm websocket_service's retry loop at lines 133-154 treats arbitrary exceptions as reconnect triggers and not fatal task crashes.
changelog/3233.fixed.md has '\ No newline at end of file'. Most repos enforce a trailing newline via lint/pre-commit. Add one to avoid CI noise and consistent file hygiene.

issues.description: Some 'error' message types may not be true errors and shouldn't push_error
issues.detail: Types like 'commit_throttled', 'insufficient_audio_activity', and 'rate_limited' are arguably informational/backpressure signals rather than hard errors. Pushing them as ErrorFrames could trigger downstream error handlers or pipeline shutdown in user code. Consider splitting into warning vs. error tiers, or confirm with ElevenLabs docs that all listed types should be treated identically.

review.summary: The PR correctly identifies a real bug (outer try/except swallowing disconnect exceptions and causing an infinite reconnect loop) and broadens error-type coverage. The fix to remove _process_messages indirection is clean. Main concerns: the consolidation drops per-type logger.error calls (regression in observability), 'transcriber_error' is duplicated in the tuple, several listed types are informational rather than errors and may over-trigger downstream error handling, and the changelog file lacks a trailing newline. Also worth verifying push_error's expected signature accepts a plain string given the PR description references ErrorFrames.
